analysis.title: Credit Supply Outlook 2027
key_insights: ING forecasts EUR corporate supply at €444bn in 2027, about 8.5% below the 2026 record of €485bn. Net supply is €126bn after redemptions rise to €318bn, the first decline in net supply in several years.

Drivers of the easing in EUR corporate supply are higher rates, slightly wider spreads, steeper curves, hyperscaler fatigue and a more volatile backdrop. EUR IG all-in yields are back near 4.5%, driven by underlying rates rather than wider spreads.

TMT dominates EUR corporate supply: gross €150bn in 2027 (vs €125bn in 2026) and net €103bn after €47bn of redemptions. Utilities are forecast at €75bn gross (€80bn in 2026) and €35bn net (€44bn in 2026).

EUR bank bond supply is forecast at €450bn in 2027 (€455bn in 2026). Redemptions near €400bn are the highest in a decade, with covered bond maturities at a record €186bn. Net bank supply is €57bn vs €89bn in 2026.
Bank supply by segment for 2027: covered €185bn, senior unsecured €210bn (€70bn senior preferred, €140bn bail-in), subordinated €55bn (Tier 2 €35bn, AT1 €20bn).

Senior preferred supply is forecast down €10bn y/y. The CMDI reforms, expected in 2028, could make senior preferred less attractive than senior bail-in because preferred would rank below uncovered deposits.

ING's economists expect an additional ECB rate hike in 2026, taking policy rates to 2.75% in early 2027. Eurozone GDP growth is forecast at 1.5% in 2H27. ING does not expect this backdrop to lift bank bond supply.

Geopolitics is a risk to spreads: the March 2026 US-Israel conflict with Iran caused brief volatility, French budget and OAT-Bund concerns have widened spreads again, and a broader Middle East escalation could add pressure. ING does not see these as a strong negative for bank bond supply.

USD corporate supply is forecast at about US$1tr in 2027, below the record-like US$1.1tr in 2020 and 2026. Redemptions are US$553bn and net supply is about US$447bn, a heavier net burden than in EUR. USD IG 5yr all-in yield is near 5.2%.

Hyperscalers have raised about US$237bn across currencies in 2026 (US$160bn in USD, US$31bn in EUR), led by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle and IBM. ING forecasts about US$280bn in 2027 (about US$190bn USD, US$65bn/€60bn EUR). Other tech adds about US$200bn.

USD TMT supply is forecast at US$425bn gross and US$304bn net in 2027. Utilities are US$160bn gross and US$99bn net. Healthcare (US$90bn) and Industrials (US$120bn) have sizeable gross supply offset by redemptions.

Reverse Yankee supply is forecast at €100bn in 2027, matching 2026. Hyperscalers account for about €60bn (up from about €31bn), leaving only about €40bn from other borrowers because the cross-currency swap economics have deteriorated. Reverse Yankee is 12% of US corporate and 23% of EUR corporate issuance, up from 10-11% and 20-21%.

Corporate hybrid supply is forecast at €35bn in 2027, down from a record 2026 (€46bn market). First calls are €23bn (true refinancing need about €19bn, €25bn with early 2028 refinancing), plus about €10bn from utility capex, rating defence, M&A and Moody's 30NC structure. Higher rates are the main downside risk.
Moody's 30NC hybrid format accounted for €15bn (32%) of 2026 hybrid issuance. It sits one notch below the Basic Credit Assessment and gets IFRS debt accounting rather than equity accounting.

ING expects hyperscaler EBITDA (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle) to grow US$230bn, or 29%, to about US$1tr in FY27, and hyperscaler capex to approach US$1tr. ING is not yet concerned about credit quality, though off-balance-sheet lease commitments are a caveat and ING prefers to wait for the 10-K filings.

Tech issuers are a small share of EUR benchmarks (Alphabet 1.16%, Amazon 0.68%, IBM 0.91% of iBoxx € Non-Financials) vs Oracle above 2% in the iBoxx $ index. ING sees room for more tech supply in EUR, and says €150bn gross is close to what the European market can absorb. TMT spreads look attractive relative to ratings, with widening driven by supply and liquidity.

Sustainable bank bond supply is above €86bn YTD (up almost €20bn y/y) and is forecast at €100bn in 2027 (22% of EUR bank supply), with green €85bn including €17bn under the EU Green Bond Standard. Sustainable redemptions rise to €67bn.
Corporate ESG supply is forecast at €72bn in 2027 (€70bn in 2026), with net supply €41bn. Utilities are 66% of 2026 ESG issuance, and about 25% of their sustainable issuance is in hybrids.

sector_views.rationale: Strong supply of €150bn gross driven by global tech AI and data centre funding. ING says spreads look attractive versus ratings, with widening driven by technicals rather than credit risk.
Supply stays high at €75bn on capex above €200bn, with German names up about 30% y/y. Hybrid issuance is at the highest since 2015.
Supply stays elevated at €450bn on record redemptions, with a modest macro backdrop adding no further impetus.

macro_indicators.reading: 2.75% in early 2027 after an additional hike in 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: ING economists' forecast. Higher policy rates raise issuers' cost of debt and are not expected to boost lending growth.
Slight pick-up but well below post-pandemic levels, so not a catalyst for bank bond supply.
Higher underlying rates, not wider spreads, drove the rise, which supports demand for credit.
Higher rates keep yields attractive but raise the cost of debt for issuers.

risk_factors: Higher rates and rising debt costs could cut hybrid issuance and moderate M&A-related issuance as 2027 progresses.
Hyperscaler lease commitments not yet on balance sheet could draw more rating agency weight if returns on investment decline.
Hyperscaler fatigue and weaker Reverse Yankee economics could reduce EUR supply from US issuers.
Middle East escalation and French political uncertainty could cause periods of spread volatility.
EU ESG simplification (narrower CSRD scope) could make it harder for banks to identify assets eligible for sustainable bonds.
Large tech supply may exceed what the European market can absorb above about €150bn gross for TMT.
vol_and_positioning: Asset swap spreads on bank bonds recovered quickly after the March volatility to levels near historical lows, then widened again on French and fiscal concerns. Periodic widening may make banks less keen to pre-fund 2028 redemptions.
Spreads on EUR TMT are wide relative to ratings, and relatively wide CDS spreads suggest technical factors rather than credit deterioration are weighing on valuations.
geopolitical: US-Israel conflict with Iran from March 2026 caused brief spread volatility. A broader Middle East escalation with no clear resolution could pressure spreads.
French budget and political concerns and OAT-Bund volatility, plus broader European fiscal concerns, have widened spreads recently.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler EBITDA is expected to grow 29% to about US$1tr in FY27, most have limited net debt and Microsoft holds more cash than debt, and spreads look attractive relative to ratings.
tension_points.bear_case: Lease commitments not yet on balance sheets, possible rating agency scrutiny if returns decline, and hyperscaler fatigue could cut supply appetite or widen spreads.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Declining returns on investment, or rating agencies giving greater weight to lease liabilities, once the 10-K filings are published.

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscalers and the wider tech sector remain major drivers of issuance in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: Hyperscalers and the wider technology sector will remain key drivers of funding activity

theme_stances.key_argument: First decline in net supply in several years provides a more supportive technical backdrop for credit spreads.
theme_stances.evidence: providing a more supportive technical backdrop for credit spreads
